is_anopheles.evidence: The study was conducted on the red flour beetle, Tribolium castaneum (strain GA-1), to investigate the function of G protein-coupled receptors via RNA interference (e.g., Title, Abstract, and Methods section 'Beetle rearing and staging'). Anopheles gambiae is only mentioned in the introduction and discussion as background context.

reports_target_markers.evidence: No insecticide resistance target markers were genotyped; the study is a functional genomic RNAi screen of GPCRs in Tribolium castaneum.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No marker genotype frequencies or counts are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: No African field populations of mosquitoes were used; the study used laboratory strain GA-1 of Tribolium castaneum.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article detailing an empirical RNAi screen in beetles.

sub_country_location.evidence: Not applicable; no field mosquito populations were studied.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Not applicable; no field mosquito collections were performed.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study does not utilize mosquito datasets.

supplement.evidence: The paper does not involve target marker data in mosquitoes; supplementary files contain Tribolium GPCR alignments and screening mortality tables.

assessment.summary: This study is an RNAi screen of G protein-coupled receptors in the red flour beetle Tribolium castaneum to identify potential pesticide targets. It does not evaluate Anopheles mosquitoes or genotype any insecticide resistance markers.
exclusion_reasons: Studies Tribolium castaneum, not Anopheles mosquitoes.
Does not genotype any insecticide-resistance target markers.
No African field-collected mosquito populations tested.
